label: Twitch
terms_note: POST /helix/chat/messages — user token with user:write:chat, or app token with user:bot + channel:bot (broadcaster-authorised; gives the Chat Bot badge). Chat limits: 20 messages / 30 s for regular accounts, 100 / 30 s for broadcaster / mods / VIPs, verified bots 7,500 / 30 s, always ≤1 message per second per channel when not mod / VIP; Send Chat Message has its own rate-limit bucket; Helix generally 800 points / minute token bucket. Whispers: POST /helix/whispers, scope user:manage:whispers, verified phone number, 40 unique recipients / day, 3 / s and 100 / min, may be silently dropped; verified bots get no higher whisper limits. Read chat via EventSub channel.chat.message (app token + channel:bot).

sdks: Helix is plain HTTPS; community libs (twitchio, tmi.js) — dev.twitch.tv

tools.name: list_inbound
tools.endpoint: EventSub `channel.chat.message` (websocket or webhook transport) — there is no chat-history REST endpoint

endpoints.call: POST /helix/chat/messages` `{broadcaster_id, sender_id, message, reply_parent_message_id}` → `{message_id, is_sent, drop_reason}
endpoints.notes: separate bucket; 20 msgs / 30 s regular, 100 / 30 s broadcaster / mod / VIP, 7,500 / 30 s verified bots; ≤ 1 / s per channel when not mod / VIP
40 unique recipients / day, 3 / s, 100 / min, may be silently dropped; verified bots get no more

reference.limits: - Helix general: 800 points / minute token bucket per client id / token. 429 → `Ratelimit-Reset`. - Chat is public; whispers are the only private lane and are intentionally throttled — never a campaign channel. Developer Agreement forbids spam / unsolicited whispers.

adapter.rate_note: Whispers: at most 40 unique recipients per day, 3 per second and 100 per minute (429 above); chat messages follow chat limits (20 per 30 s as a regular user).

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: Twitch app client id (dev.twitch.tv console); also sent as the Client-Id header on every Helix call.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: Twitch app client secret (form body of the refresh request to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token).

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: User refresh token from the authorization-code flow with scopes user:manage:whispers and user:write:chat. Twitch may return a new refresh token: the runtime keeps it in memory and, with PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR set, saves it to <dir>/twitch.json (mode 0600). The state file is keyed by platform id, so it is shared with social/twitch: give each server its own PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR (or its own consent / refresh token) so the two never race on one single-use refresh token.

config_fields.name: sender_id
config_fields.help: User id of the token's user (GET /helix/users with the token): from_user_id of whispers and sender_id of chat replies. It 'must match the user ID in the user access token'; the account needs a verified phone number to whisper.

config_fields.name: broadcaster_id
config_fields.help: User id of the channel whose chat reply posts into (needed only for reply).

me.note: Get Users without ids returns the token's user (account.data[0]: id, login, display_name).

send.note: Send Whisper: `to` is the recipient's Twitch user id (not a login). 204 on success - 'The API may silently drop whispers that it suspects of violating Twitch policies ... it returns a 204 status code as if it succeeded', so status 'sent' is not a delivery receipt. Max 500 characters to a user who has not whispered you before (10,000 otherwise; longer is truncated). No message id is returned; `subject` and `channel` are ignored.

reply.note: Replies in config broadcaster_id's chat to the chat message `thread_id` (reply_parent_message_id); `channel` is ignored. A message blocked by AutoMod or chat settings answers 200 with raw.is_sent=false and raw.drop_reason - check is_sent.

not_offered.list_inbound: Helix has no endpoint to read whispers or chat; they arrive only through EventSub (user.whisper.message, channel.chat.message; https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/eventsub/eventsub-subscription-types/).
not_offered.get_thread: There is no whisper or chat history endpoint in Helix (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/api/reference/); history exists only in EventSub deliveries.
not_offered.mark_read: Twitch exposes no read-state for whispers or chat (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/api/reference/).

evidence: probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 2/3 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages, 1 by their last segments; names not found on the page: send:from_user_id, send:to_user_id
